proposals.title: Integrative Correction of Mis-assigned Spots via Expression and Spatial Geometry
proposals.summary: This proposal focuses on detecting and correcting mis-assigned spots by integrating dimensionality reduction techniques with spatial neighborhood graph analyses. It employs statistical frameworks that leverage both expression similarity and spatial distances to identify spots that diverge from local profiles. The approach applies neighbor-based correction while preserving genuine biological heterogeneity and includes validation through differential expression analyses and spatial visualizations to confirm improvements in marker specificity and spatial domain integrity.

proposals.title: Discrimination of Tissue versus Background in Spatial Transcriptomics
proposals.summary: This analysis targets the challenge of distinguishing between actual tissue regions and background noise in spatial transcriptomics data. By integrating morphological cues with gene expression profiles and spatial statistics, the method quantifies the differences between tissue and non-tissue spots. Rigorous quality control metrics are applied to flag ambiguous or low-confidence background spots, ensuring that subsequent analyses focus on true biological signals. Validation is performed by comparing spatial enrichment patterns to known tissue boundaries and gold-standard regions.

proposals.title: Automated Detection and Filtering of Low-Quality Spots
proposals.summary: This proposal is designed to identify and remove low-quality spots that may confound downstream analyses. It applies a suite of quality control metrics—including signal-to-noise ratios, coverage depths, and expression uniformity—combined with spatial consistency checks. Low-quality spots are flagged before further analysis, and their impact is evaluated through controlled perturbations. The method is validated using known quality benchmarks and by assessing improvements in spatial clustering, marker gene specificity, and overall data integrity.

proposals.title: Benchmarking Correction Methods on Mixtures and Gold Standard Annotations
proposals.summary: This study establishes a rigorous evaluation framework by benchmarking correction strategies on datasets with known species mixtures or gold-standard tissue annotations. The proposal includes systematic cross-validation of spatial correction algorithms against controlled mixtures, assessing performance improvements in marker gene specificity, spatial domain clarity, and cell-type calls. Statistical tests and visual assessments are used to compare corrected versus uncorrected data, ensuring that the adjustments do not obscure genuine biological heterogeneity.

proposals.title: Sensitivity-Tuned Detection and Correction of Outlier Spots
proposals.summary: This analysis emphasizes the detection of outlier spots that may represent either rare cell states or artifacts due to contamination. By applying sensitivity-tuned divergence metrics and statistical outlier tests within a spatial context, the approach discriminates true biological variation from correction targets. The method combines neighbor-based smoothing with adaptive thresholds that respect tissue boundaries, ensuring that only genuine artifacts are corrected. Comprehensive validation is achieved through differential expression analysis and quantitative assessments against benchmark datasets.

proposals.title: Robust Correction Strategy for Mixed-Cell Capture Artifacts
proposals.summary: Focusing on the challenge of mixed-cell capture, this proposal integrates rigorous quality control, dimensionality reduction, and spatial graph analyses to repair artifacts caused by spot contamination. The method combines quantitative divergence metrics with an adaptive neighbor-based correction algorithm, ensuring accurate re-assignment of expression profiles. Emphasis is placed on preserving real biological signals while mitigating cross-boundary contamination, with validation performed through side-by-side visual and statistical comparisons against gold-standard annotations.

proposals.title: Refinement of Spatial Domains via Adaptive Neighbor Smoothing
proposals.summary: This proposal employs adaptive neighbor smoothing techniques to refine spatial domain definitions and improve marker specificity. By constructing spatial neighborhood graphs that respect tissue geometry and leveraging statistical smoothing algorithms, the approach corrects local expression artifacts without oversmoothing true biological variability. Sensitivity analyses are conducted to calibrate spatial thresholds and validate the method’s performance. Subsequent differential expression and visualization analyses confirm enhanced spatial coherence and distinct domain boundaries.

proposals.title: Comprehensive Spatial Quality Control Framework for Transcriptomics
proposals.summary: This final proposal outlines an integrated framework that combines the detection of mis-assigned spots, tissue versus background discrimination, and low-quality spot filtering into a unified spatial quality control pipeline. The analysis incorporates multiple layers of statistical testing, spatial graph modeling, and rigorous benchmarking against controlled mixtures and gold standards. By systematically addressing each quality issue with tailored correction strategies, the approach ensures a refined dataset that enhances downstream analyses such as cell-type classification, spatial domain identification, and marker gene specificity.

plan.user_request: Coordinate agents to propose, critique, and finalize exactly 8 computational spatial-omics analyses likely performed in a hidden spatial transcriptomics paper, producing only JSON proposal artifacts.

steps.title: Draft spatial-CV analysis proposals
steps.description: Have the Spatial-CV Planning Agent (`spatial_cv_agent`) use the public background on spatial QC in spot-based sequencing spatial transcriptomics to draft a set of exactly 8 computational spatial-omics analysis proposals most likely performed in the hidden paper. Each proposal should be a candidate analysis (not executed), described with an internal title and detailed summary, and all 8 should be written as a JSON draft to `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json`.
steps.reasoning: This step leverages the spatial_cv_agent’s expertise to translate the background problem (spot mixing, contamination, spatial QC, and boundary sharpening) into concrete but still tentative computational analysis ideas, establishing a structured draft that downstream agents can critique and refine.
steps.assignment_rationale: Step 1 must be handled by the Spatial-CV Planning Agent, which is explicitly designed to draft exactly 8 spatial analysis proposals and write them to hypotheses/draft_proposals.json (with an audited spatial_cv_proposals copy).

steps.title: Critique draft proposals
steps.description: Have the Critic agent read `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and evaluate the 8 draft proposals for plausibility, distinctness, coverage of the spatial QC problem, and alignment with the public background (e.g., detection/repair of misassigned spots, use of expression plus geometry, evaluation on mixtures or gold standards). The Critic should not design new analyses or execute any, but instead produce a structured written critique with per-proposal comments and overall recommendations, saving it to `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json`.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated critique step ensures that the candidate analyses are coherent, non-redundant, and well-targeted to the stated challenges (contamination, boundaries, QC dependencies) before they are finalized, providing explicit guidance for revision while maintaining the original 8-proposal structure.
steps.assignment_rationale: Step 2 is a pure review step producing hypotheses/critique.json, which matches the critic_agent’s advertised role as a review-only critic that writes only critique.json and does not generate or revise proposals.

steps.title: Synthesize final proposal set
steps.description: Have the Hypothesis agent read both `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json` and then synthesize a final set of exactly 8 computational spatial-omics analysis proposals. The agent should revise titles and summaries as needed for clarity, distinctness, and fidelity to the public background, but must not execute any analyses. It must write `project/outputs/hypotheses/final_proposals.json` as a JSON object whose only top-level key is `proposals`, containing an array of 8 items, where each item has only `title` and a detailed `summary` of the proposed analysis.
steps.reasoning: This final synthesis step integrates the initial spatial-CV-driven ideas with the Critic’s feedback to produce a polished, non-redundant, and well-justified set of 8 proposals, encoded in the exact JSON structure required for downstream use.
steps.assignment_rationale: Step 3 requires integrating the draft and critique to produce the finalized set of 8 proposals in hypotheses/final_proposals.json, which is exactly the hypothesis_agent’s role as the specialist for drafting and final synthesis of spatial paper analyses.

provenance.justification: Existing templates (e.g., paper_hypothesis_generation, hypothesis_testing) are oriented toward executing computational analyses or full paper-plus-data workflows, whereas this task is a constrained three-step TA+CV proposal-synthesis pipeline that must only generate, critique, and finalize eight analysis proposals as JSON artifacts without running any analyses. Therefore, a custom minimal plan was created to meet the user’s exact structural and agent-assignment requirements.
